title: Gym Bag Essentials
meta_desc: Get the most out of your gym sessions with our practical guide on what to pack in your gym bag, including essentials and tips for NZ gym-goers
intro: Heading to the gym can be daunting, especially when it comes to packing the right gear. As a beginner, it's essential to know what to bring and what your gym will provide. In this guide, we'll cover the must-haves for your gym bag, so you can focus on your fitness journey. Most NZ gyms, including City Fitness and Les Mills, offer basic amenities, but it's always best to be prepared.

sections.heading: Clothing and Footwear
sections.body: When it comes to clothing and footwear, it's crucial to choose items that are comfortable and suitable for your workout. A good pair of sneakers or cross-trainers is a must, and moisture-wicking clothing can help keep you cool and dry. Consider the type of exercises you'll be doing and dress accordingly. For example, if you're planning a yoga or Pilates session, you may want to wear stretchy clothing that allows for a full range of motion.

sections.heading: Towels and Toiletries
sections.body: Most NZ gyms provide towels, but it's always a good idea to bring your own, especially if you have sensitive skin. You should also pack any necessary toiletries, such as deodorant, shampoo, and conditioner. If you plan on showering at the gym, consider bringing a small towel and a toiletry bag to keep your belongings organized.

sections.heading: Water and Snacks
sections.body: Staying hydrated is essential, especially during intense workouts. Bring a refillable water bottle to ensure you have enough water throughout your session. Some gyms, like Jetts and Anytime Fitness, offer water fountains, but it's still a good idea to bring your own. You may also want to pack a snack, such as a protein bar or fruit, to keep your energy levels up.

sections.heading: Lockers and Storage
sections.body: When using the lockers at your gym, make sure to bring a lock to secure your belongings. Some gyms, like City Fitness, offer digital locks, but it's still a good idea to bring your own. Consider packing a small bag with essentials, such as your phone, wallet, and keys, and keep it with you during your workout. Don't forget to check with your gym about their storage policies and any additional fees.

sections.heading: Additional Tips
sections.body: Finally, consider packing any additional items that will enhance your workout experience, such as a fitness tracker or headphones. Some gyms, like Les Mills, offer group fitness classes, so you may want to bring a towel to wipe down equipment. Don't forget to check with your gym about their policies on food and drink, as well as any specific rules for certain areas of the gym. If you're looking for a more affordable gym option, consider Exercise NZ's subsidised gym scheme, which offers 40-70% off membership prices.
